clue.text: A-lister's cool futuristic vehicle

blocks.note: an A-lister is a star; the possessive 's is kept
hip means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A celebrity shows off a sleek, space-age car.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s on the celebrity stays in the answer as a plain S, so STAR'S runs straight into HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A starship is a spacecraft for interstellar travel, the stock vehicle of science fiction.

clue.text: Exceptional whistle-blower is great on turf

blocks.note: super means great, excellent
turf is grass

explanation.surface: An outstanding informer shines when playing on a grass pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. A grass is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A supergrass is British slang for an informer who betrays many criminals at once, hence an exceptional one.

clue.text: Clean six-footer having one month in charge

blocks.note: an insect has six feet, and the ant is the crossword's favourite
the Roman numeral for one
the short form of September
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A tall, tidy person has spent a month running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something antiseptic is free of germs, so thoroughly sterile and clean.

clue.text: Creature written about in Italian sonnet

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
about means turned round, so the letters are set down back to front

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A poet writes a sonnet in Italian about some animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs backwards across the join of the two words, reading from the end of 'sonnet' back into 'Italian'.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail is a slow-moving shelled mollusc, a specific example of a living creature.

clue.text: Awkward naked fiend in popular religious establishment

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go and the middle stays
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: in means fashionable, popular
a convent is a house of nuns
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An embarrassing scene: a naked devil turns up in a fashionable church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naked' sounds like the devil is unclothed, but it strips the word of its outer letters; the remainder slips in just before the last letter of the religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconvenient causes trouble or difficulty, a close synonym of awkward in the sense of ill-timed.

clue.text: Bits of cold strange US rubbish

blocks.note: C for cold, as on a tap
rum is British slang for odd, strange
BS is American slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: Odd cold scraps of American garbage lie about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like an anagram signal but it is the word RUM, old British slang for odd. BS abbreviates an American vulgarism for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumbs are small fragments, typically of bread or cake, so tiny pieces or bits.

clue.text: Boar's feet prepared for Sunday lunch?

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked over, so these letters are made into something new

blocks.note: taken as written, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: Pig's trotters are cooked for the weekend family meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cooking a boar's trotters; the S of the apostrophe is part of the fodder. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast beef is the traditional British Sunday dinner, so it is one example of a Sunday lunch.

clue.text: Medium upset couple

blocks.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
as in 'what's eating him?', to eat is to bother, so ate means upset

explanation.surface: A psychic distresses a pair of clients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the past tense of eat in the sense 'what's eating you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mate is to pair up or join together, so as a verb it means to couple.

clue.text: Various cabbages have skin disease

indicators.note: to have is to hold or contain, so the letters are held within the words before

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word joined to the opening three of the second

explanation.surface: Several kinds of cabbage are suffering from a blight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' looks like an anagram signal, but the answer simply sits across the join of the two words. The definition fits plants as well as people, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Scab names a crusty patch on a wound and also several fungal diseases of plants and animal skin.

clue.text: Inept act reformed miserable wage

indicators.note: something reformed has been made over into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bungled performance gets the actor a pitiful fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inept act' reads as a description of a bad show; it is only letters for rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a very small or inadequate amount of money paid as salary or allowance.

clue.text: Bloke with revolutionary knack for incantation

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word is set down backwards

blocks.note: a bloke is a man
an art is a knack or skill

explanation.surface: A radical with a gift for casting spells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a political description of the bloke, but it turns the skill round.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a sacred word or chant repeated in meditation, close to a spoken spell or chant.

clue.text: Subordinate part in inferior play

blocks.note: second-rate, lower in rank, so inferior
to fiddle is to play idly or fidget

explanation.surface: A minor role in a poor stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all theatre, a small part in a bad play, but 'play' is a verb, as in to play with something.
explanation.definitionFit: To play second fiddle is to take a lesser role, from the junior violin part in an orchestra.

clue.text: Magnificent piano left on purpose in here with front missing

indicators.note: placed on means set right next to, so the short pieces are joined in sequence
the front is the first letter, and missing means it has been dropped
to be in something is to sit inside it, so one group goes within the other

blocks.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
L is the standard abbreviation for left
an end is an aim or purpose
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: Someone has deliberately left a splendid piano in this room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here' looks like a place, but it means in attendance, as in 'present and correct'; that word loses its first letter and wraps round the three short pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Resplendent describes something splendid, dazzling and impressive in appearance, a direct synonym of magnificent.

clue.text: Mother's nag about missing lid on sage sauce

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is written back to front
the lid is the top, in a down clue the first letter, and missing means it is gone

blocks.note: an informal word for mother
to nag someone is to pester or annoy them
a sage is wise

explanation.surface: A mother complains about the herb sauce lacking its lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sage' looks like the herb going into the sauce, but it is a wise person, giving WISE before it loses its top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is a thick cold dressing made from egg yolk and oil, a common example of a sauce.

clue.text: Lowering of Parisian somewhere below ground

blocks.note: de is French for of
a basement is a floor beneath ground level

explanation.surface: Lowering a Parisian into an underground room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of Parisian' means the French word for of, a common crossword device for foreign small words.
explanation.definitionFit: Debasement is the reduction of quality or value, a moral or monetary degrading, which is a lowering.

clue.text: Mature heads of Royal Institution promote educational networks

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top, so only the opening letter of each is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Senior figures at a scientific body push learning networks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Institution is a London science body, which makes 'heads' look like its directors; here it picks out first letters from the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to grow fully developed, as fruit does, which is to mature.

clue.text: Villainous foe ruins a broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wicked enemy wrecks a television transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' reads as a programme being ruined, but in its old sense of scattering it signals the letter shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means wicked or criminal, a close formal synonym of villainous.

clue.text: A traitor enters river to get clear

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a means one
a rat is someone who betrays others
the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: A turncoat wades into a river to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is not just an article: it becomes the number one. The Exe is a river in south-west England, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to free someone from blame, which is to clear their name.

clue.text: Tried firs chopped up and cooked

indicators.note: food that is chopped up is cut into pieces and mixed, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to cut up fir trees and make dinner of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped up' fits the trees in the surface, as if felled for logs, but it is the cue to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir-fried food has been fried quickly in a wok while stirred, one particular way of being cooked.

clue.text: Vegetation initially found living on restricted area

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Plants first discovered growing inside a fenced-off zone.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue reads like a botanist's note; every word after 'initially' contributes its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the collective term for the plant life of a region, a synonym of vegetation.

clue.text: New dawn as rains cease spreading across North

indicators.note: spreading things out loosens their order, so these letters are rearranged
to lie across something is to straddle it, so the letters surround another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A fresh morning breaks as the northern rain finally stops.
explanation.walkthrough: The weather surface makes 'New dawn' look literal; it defines a figurative rebirth.
explanation.definitionFit: A renaissance is a revival or rebirth of activity, figuratively a fresh start or new beginning.

clue.text: Begin small pastry dish

blocks.note: S is the size abbreviation for small
a tart is a pastry case with a filling

explanation.surface: Someone begins on a little pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' looks like it describes the pastry, but it gives its own abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To start is to commence or set going, a direct synonym of begin as a verb.

clue.text: Parasite in rotten leaf

indicators.note: something rotten has decayed out of shape, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bug lurks in a decaying leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it places the parasite inside the leaf, but it just links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small wingless insect that feeds on blood, a typical example of a parasite.

clue.text: Regularly dissolve something in water

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every second letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A routine instruction to dissolve some powder in water.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a chemistry step; the definition is the vague 'something in water', which is fair because land surrounded by sea is just that.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, land that sits surrounded by sea or lake, hence a thing in water.

clue.text: Instruction in reduced working

blocks.note: less means reduced, diminished
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Guidance on how to work part-time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a period of teaching, so a piece of instruction given to a learner.

clue.text: Glorify ladies dancing around island before start of evening

indicators.note: dancers move around and change places, so the letters take a new order
around means encircling, so one piece wraps another
the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is taken
before means coming first, so the pieces are joined in that order

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Admirers praise women dancing on an island as night falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes inside the jumbled LADIES, and the E from 'evening' closes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To idealise is to regard something as perfect, better than it really is, which is to glorify it.

clue.text: Hostile part of song

blocks.note: first meaning: opposed to or strongly disliking something
second meaning, read as two words: one stanza of a song, with the article in front

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning only works if the answer is split after its first letter, as the article plus a stanza.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse means strongly disliking or opposing something, so having a hostile attitude to it.

clue.text: Aware male is lacking in feeling

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
sentiment is a feeling or emotion

explanation.surface: A perceptive man nonetheless shows no emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints an unfeeling man; actually the M for male is what goes missing from the feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentient being can perceive and feel things, so it is conscious or aware of its surroundings.
